## Summary

A checklist for making repos fast for *agents* (and humans) — framed as "send this to your agent :)":

- **Faster runners** (e.g. ex-Blacksmith class) — the chart shows ~2 min per PR burned just *waiting for a machine*, inside an ~11 min job (≈70s lint, ≈33s typecheck, <5s test shard once isolated, ≈35s checkout, ≈12–13s install/deps — OCR-approximate).
- **Oxlint** replacing ESLint, **`bun check`/bun for tsc** — linter/typecheck engine swaps.
- **Bigger test machines + Vitest isolation OFF** — throw hardware at it instead of paying isolation overhead.
- **Fix caching, blobless clones** (`git clone --filter=blob:none`) — checkout and dep-install are pure waste when cacheable.
- **Parallel jobs + `nx affected`** — only build/test what changed.
- **Pre-push hooks** — catch before CI minutes burn.

## Why it matters

- The pitch is agent-era: agents burn CI cycles iterating, so per-PR latency and queue time compound into agent wall-clock — the same "buy back attention" logic this vault applies to life, applied to build pipelines.
- Most items presume a monorepo with real CI (runners, nx, Vitest). Our repos are small script/report repos with no CI matrix — the *transferable* subset is: pre-push hooks, blobless/partial clones on big-history repos, and caching installs.
- **Skepticism gates:** the full checklist sits behind a login-gated X article (known dead end from this host — content unfetchable at capture; only the TL;DR + chart are verified). Numbers on the chart are OCR-approximate; "bun check for tsc" is a tooling claim worth verifying per-repo, not a drop-in.
- Task filed: triage which items apply to our own repos (Inbox).
